speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help diagnose your chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and have you noticed any blood or mucus in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the camping history, have you noticed any weight loss, fever, or nighttime awakenings due to diarrhea? I will also request stool studies to rule out infectious causes like Giardia. REQUEST TEST: Stool_Ova_and_Parasites

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the stool studies were normal and your symptoms are relieved by defecation, do you experience any changes in the frequency or form of your stool related to stress or specific foods? I will also request a colonoscopy to rule out inflammatory bowel disease. REQUEST TEST: Colonoscopy

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the colonoscopy is normal and symptoms are relieved by defecation, do you experience bloating or abdominal distension, and does your stool consistency change significantly with stress or specific foods? REQUEST TEST: Breath_Hydrogen

speaker: Doctor
text: With negative results for infection, inflammation, and lactose intolerance, your symptoms strongly suggest Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS). Do you have any family history of IBS or other functional gastrointestinal disorders?

speaker: Doctor
text: That detail about your camping companion falling ill is concerning and suggests a potential missed infectious etiology despite the normal initial stool test. I will request a repeat stool PCR panel to specifically screen for bacterial pathogens like Campylobacter or Salmonella. REQUEST TEST: Stool_PCR_Panel

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal infectious workup and the specific symptom of relief with defecation, your presentation is classic for Irritable Bowel Syndrome with diarrhea (IBS-D). I will now confirm this diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Irritable Bowel Syndrome with diarrhea (IBS-D)
